steps.title: Use the complete Windows package
steps.instruction: The managed Windows route keeps RoadRash64Recompiled.exe with its official assets, libraries and importer tools, and prepares your matching USA v1.0 original through Core. Linux experimental AppImage packages have different storage and upstream installation instructions; the Windows contract does not establish their managed support or native qualification.

steps.title: Keep optional setup with the game
steps.instruction: Optional texture, character and Mario Kart 64 course imports remain deliberate upstream features. Follow the included guide and supply an extra original only if you choose that feature. Portcove does not discover and run the DirectStart or importer helpers automatically. Close the game and importer before replacing a runtime. Preserve the complete local race-packs folder, including import jobs and previous-pack backups; custom external course-pack folders require a separate backup.

steps.title: Keep your current copy while changing routes
steps.instruction: A historical managed v1.4.3 copy retains its accepted definition and data locations. Keep it usable while a supported transition is unavailable. For a separately prepared or customized upstream copy, select the completed player in its own stable folder, save launch details, then choose Play separately. Upstream or you provide that external copy’s runtime updates; Portcove registration removal leaves every external file untouched and does not grant managed Backup or Rollback.

presentation.manual_preparation: Supply your own matching Road Rash 64 USA v1.0 original. Core verifies it and prepares the canonical ROM beside the Windows portable player. This route preserves declared settings, saves, mods, custom music and local imported race packs, including importer logs and previous-pack backups beneath race-packs. Close the game and any importer before updates or backups. Custom external pack paths, including RR64_PRIVATE_COURSE_PACK, remain outside managed backups. Runtime rollback carries current declared data; it does not rewind progress or establish old-reader compatibility. Historical v1.4.3 installations retain their wrapper-prefixed contract: a changed data-coordinate transition remains held until supported, so keep the working copy and its data.
